newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN SOCCER FANS SET STANDS ABLAZE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN SOCCER FANS SET STANDS ABLAZE.

text.p: Romanian soccer fans set fire to stands before the start of a match between two rival Bucharest teams on Saturday, destroying hundreds of seats and prompting police to evacuate 2,000 spectators, officials said.

Fans resisting the evacuation fought with police posted at the Steaua stadium in anticipation of trouble. About 30 were arrested and the match pitting first division Steaua against Dinamo Bucharest was briefly delayed. There were no serious injuries.

Marcel Puscas, President of Steaua, told Reuters that about 700 seats were destroyed after the fire broke out 10 minutes before the scheduled kick-off with about 16,000 fans watching. The game, delayed for no more than five minutes, was eventually won 3-1 by Steaua.
"After the evacuation, police near the stadium questioned large groups of fans to determine who had caused the trouble," Puscas told Reuters.
"The vast majority of the 2,000 fans evacuated and the 30 now in detention are teenagers."

Soccer violence has worsened in Romania in the seven years since the end of Communist rule. Steaua, the traditional military team, and Dinamo, representing the police, have a long history of rivalry, with clashes frequently erupting between rival supporters.
